true_answer: (Remember, the order the elements are written down in does not matter.) Also, { 1 , 2 , 3 } | { 1 , 1 + 1 , 1 + 1 + 1 } | { I , II , III } | { 1 , 2 , 3 , 1 + 2 } since these are all ways to write the set containing the first three positive integers (how we write them doesn’t matter, just what they are). What about the sets A | { 1 , 2 , 3 } and B | { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } ? Clearly A , B , but notice that every element of A is also an element of B . Because of this we say that A is a subset of B , or in symbols A ⊂ B or A ⊆ B .
